name: Basketball-Reference

sections.note: Season-by-season and career totals. THE record for an NBA/WNBA statistic. Cite the player page, not a leaderboard, when the claim is about one player.
Correct source for 'who leads all time in X'. Volatile for active players, any card citing this needs v:1.
/teams/LAL/ is franchise history; /teams/LAL/1972.html is one season.
MVP, Finals MVP, DPOY, ROY. One page legitimately backs many cards.
The only acceptable source for a single-game claim (81 points, the Flu Game).
Same structure as the NBA side. Coverage is thinner pre-2000.
Fun pages, not records. Never cite.
Editorial. Never cite as a record.

watch_out: Career totals for ACTIVE players change nightly. Anything about a current player is volatile by definition.

name: NBA.com

sections.note: The league's own record. Equal to Basketball-Reference; prefer it for anything post-1996 where BBRef is derived.
Volatile in season.
The NBA writing ABOUT itself. Has editors, is not the record. Fine as a Tier 2 leg, never alone for a statistic. 39 rows in the bank sit here, the largest nba.com block by far.

Club sites use this instead of /news, e.g. nba.com/warriors/news-blogs/tdiwh-klay37, a This-Day-In-History post. Same thing as /news, different spelling, and the hyphen means the /news rule does not reach it.
Dated long-form, e.g. /article/2017/09/11/morning-tip-zack-clayton. Journalism.
official.nba.com/rule-no-1-court-dimensions-equipment and kin. 30 rows in the bank. This IS the record for any rules question, the league publishing its own laws.

watch_out: official.nba.com and club subdomains (nba.com/bulls/, sparks.wnba.com) follow the same rule: /stats, /history and /rule-no are records, /news and /news-blogs are journalism. THE HOLE TIERING CANNOT CLOSE: a bare slug at the root, like nba.com/top-nba-finals-moments-steve-kerr-jumper-game-6-1997-finals, is a feature article with no section in its path to give it away. It scores default_tier 1 and only a person opening it can tell. Same class of error as the BIG3 leadership page cited for the game format.

name: WNBA.com

sections.note: First stop for any WNBA statistic.

watch_out: Pre-1997 has no WNBA record because the league did not exist. Women's basketball before that needs the Women's Basketball HOF or newspaper archives.

name: Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame

sections.note: Named in the standard. THE record for induction year and class.

watch_out: A member page's career summary is a BIO, not a stat record. For a number, go to Basketball-Reference. Robert Horry's ring count on a hall page is a summary; the record is the box scores.

name: Women's Basketball Hall of Fame

sections.note: One of the very few Tier 1 sources for the women's game before 1997.

watch_out: Often the ONLY Tier 1 available for pre-1978 women's basketball. Where it is, cite it and set confidence honestly rather than dropping the history.

name: Springfield College
run_by: the college where the game was invented

sections.note: VERIFIED 2026-08-03: documents the 13 rules, the peach baskets and the 10-foot height from its own holdings and period YMCA documents.

name: NCAA
watch_out: College is OUT of V0 scope. Registered so a card citing it is recognised, not so college research starts.

name: Olympics.com

sections.note: e.g. /montreal-1976/results/basketball. This is the record.
CHECKED 2026-08-03, storytelling, not results. 'Fashion police: Lithuania and the Grateful Dead' is on this domain.

watch_out: The single clearest example of why a domain is not a document. Same site, both Tier 1 and Tier 2, decided by path.

name: BIG3

sections.note: Backs who founded the league. Does NOT back how the game is played, a card currently cites it for the format, which is a wrong-page error the tier cannot catch.

CHECKED 2026-08-03: /news/via-doombot-blog-the-basics-of-the-big3/ is bylined 'DOOMbot', a member of an NFT community. A blog on an official domain. Tier 3, not 2, this section carries outside writers with no newsroom.

watch_out: Out of V0 scope. The clearest proof that official-domain does not mean official-document.

name: Guinness World Records

sections.note: CHECKED 2026-08-03: the Mark Eaton 456-blocks page states the figure and names NO source for it. Guinness is repeating the NBA's number, not holding it. The standard says statistics are Tier 1 only, so this can never carry a stat card alone.

watch_out: Tier 1 ONLY for records Guinness adjudicates itself. For any league statistic it is a secondary reporter.

name: Wikipedia

sections.note: Never ships alone, at any count. Named in the standard.

watch_out: THE MOST IMPORTANT NAVIGATION RULE IN THIS REGISTER, and it is Aaron's own: 'Wikipedia says so is a lead, not proof, follow the citation and cite what IT cites.' 724 of the bank's sourced rows point here, by far the largest single block. Every one is a LEAD to be converted, not a citation to keep. Scroll to References, find the Basketball-Reference or league link, cite that instead.

sections.note: Named in the standard as a fan database. 52 rows in the bank point here and all of them need replacing with the league or Basketball-Reference equivalent.

name: ESPN

sections.note: Named in the standard. Needs a SECOND independent Tier 2 to carry a card.
ESPN's stats mirror official league data but ESPN is not the record. For a number, cite the league or Basketball-Reference.

watch_out: andscape.com is ESPN-owned. Two ESPN-family sources are NOT independent of each other, that pair fails the two-source rule.

name: Associated Press

sections.note: Named in the standard.

watch_out: AP copy is REPRINTED by hundreds of outlets. An AP story on ESPN and the same AP story in a local paper are ONE source, not two. Check the byline before counting a pair as independent.

name: Kos magazin
run_by: the editors of the Serbian print monthly Kos (Vladimir Stankovic, Aleksandar Ostojic)

sections.note: PLACED 2026-08-12 (V18): the electronic continuation of the print monthly Kos, same named editorial team per its o-nama page; Stankovic also wrote EuroLeague's official 101 Greats series, which is what our rows cite. RULED Tier 2 by Aaron 08-12. Foreign-language site, tiers on accountability like any other.

watch_out: Journalism, not a record of fact: stats still need Tier 1. Two independent Tier-2 sources to ship.

sections.note: PLACED 2026-08-12 (V18): its own about page says collaborators contribute freely and without compensation; no editorial accountability. RULED Tier 3 by Aaron 08-12. Its one row in the bank needs a second independent source.

name: World Dunk Association
run_by: the WDA, a community registry for competitive dunking

sections.note: An organiser is the record of its own events, the same logic that puts big3.com at Tier 1 for BIG3. RULED by Aaron 08-12.
PLACED 2026-08-12 (V18): community-driven profiles and rankings, no masthead. RULED Tier 3 default by Aaron 08-12.

watch_out: Tier 1 ONLY for its own contest results; everything else on the site is community-submitted.
